images.caption:
Scalasaig. In 2001 an outbreak of foot and mouth disease caused a sort of national hysteria. Even road cycling was portrayed as an act of criminal sabotage. 
Amongst this madness, the island of Colonsay declared that as all visitors arrived in one place, they could be disinfected, and very publicly announced that visitors were welcome. Here is the "welcome mat", ready to disinfect every visitor. Once sprayed, we were free to wander this wonderful island at will.

images.caption:
Foot and Mouth sign. Testament to the power of lamination. A nearly 6 year old sign from the epidemic of 2001.  Fortunately there were no outbreaks near here, nearest were in Liddlesdale.
There cannot be many of these signs left, as they were enthusiastically removed after things went back to normal.

images.caption:
Towards site of former Drybrook Halt, in 2001 'Foot-and- Mouth' emergency.
View SSE: an extension of the ex-GWR Newnham - Cinderford (to right) branch used to go to Drybrook Halt, but only until 7/7/30; the rest lasted until 11/58: Drybrook Halt had been in the middle distance here. The main interest is the warning sign: one's wanderings could be seriously restricted during those several months of the Emergency in 2001.
